current_formulation: A Description Logic ontology in OWL in which argument schemes are classes and scheme nodes are their instances (2011).

steps.formulation: Abstract AIF model with information nodes for claims and scheme nodes for inference, preference, and conflict.
steps.quote: There are two types of node, namely information nodes (I-nodes) and scheme application nodes or scheme nodes (S-nodes for short).

criticism.quote: in its 2006 form had not integrated modelling of dialogue

steps.formulation: AIF extended with Walton's argumentation schemes and form nodes, written in RDF Schema (AIF-RDF, ArgDF).
steps.quote: we extend the recently proposed Argument Interchange Format (AIF) to express arguments with a structure based on Walton's theory of argumentation schemes

criticism.quote: ArgDF's reification of the AIF causes some redundancy at the instance level

steps.formulation: AIF+ extends the 2006 model to dialogue: locutions map to information nodes, steps between locutions to scheme nodes.
steps.quote: This paper extends the Argument Interchange Format to enable it to represent dialogic argumentation.

steps.formulation: Description Logic ontology in OWL: schemes become classes and scheme nodes their instances.
steps.quote: The AIF model is reified by interpreting schemes as classes and S-nodes as instances of those classes
